"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 1984: a weak, mostly context-driven signal.

What it is: this component reads almost entirely from MLP hidden unit 1984 of layer 15
(its input direction is ~0.52 on that unit, and its activation correlates ~0.5 with that
unit). The unit's value depends on context rather than on which token is present: a
token's identity explains about 2% of its variance, and simple features (token class,
position, repetition, newlines, script) explain under 0.2%. Its output direction promotes
and suppresses a scattered set of unrelated tokens, so there is no single concept here.

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical value everywhere, a constant
equal to its mean activation (about 0.065), except at the first token of each document,
where the component is essentially 0. That captures the average level and nothing more.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.065


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    first_of_doc = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if first_of_doc else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Predicts layers.15.mlp.down_proj unit 1985 by document position, not by content.

This unit's activation is a linear read-out of one MLP hidden unit of layer 15 (its
down_proj direction is almost exactly that unit). That unit is spread across many
unrelated contexts (code, numbers, "no award", "->", and so on), and its value cannot
be predicted from the current token, the previous token or the token's class: each of
those explains about 1% of its variance or less on held-out text.

What is reliable is the position inside a document:
  - the first token of a document is about 0 (the unit is silent there);
  - the second token of a document is about 0.13 on average;
  - every later token averages about 0.05, the overall mean.

So the program predicts those three values. Its explained variance is near zero:
the unit has no simple readable pattern.
"""

READS = ()

FIRST_TOKEN = 0.0
SECOND_TOKEN = 0.13
OTHER_TOKENS = 0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label of the previous token, its position in that document)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    if pos == 0:
        value = FIRST_TOKEN
    elif pos == 1:
        value = SECOND_TOKEN
    else:
        value = OTHER_TOKENS
    return (doc, pos), value

"""Predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 1986.

This component is a diffuse linear readout of layer 15's MLP hidden units. Its
activation is noisy (mean -0.19, std 0.35) and is not explained by which token is
present, by the preceding token, or by position in the text: token identity explains
under 2% of its variance. Its one clear regularity is at the start of a document,
where there is almost no context: the first token reads about 0, and the second
token reads about -0.3. Everywhere else it sits near its mean of -0.19.

So the program predicts that position profile and nothing else. It tracks the
position within each document (restarting when the document label changes) and
returns 0 for the first token, -0.3 for the second, and -0.19 after that.
"""

READS = ()

START_VALUE = 0.0  # first token of a document
SECOND_VALUE = -0.30  # second token of a document
MEAN_VALUE = -0.19  # every other position


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label of the last token, number of tokens so far in that document)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        seen = 0
    else:
        seen = carry[1] + 1
    if seen == 0:
        value = START_VALUE
    elif seen == 1:
        value = SECOND_VALUE
    else:
        value = MEAN_VALUE
    return (doc, seen), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 1987: a near-silent component.

What it does: almost nothing. Its activation (its contribution to the
residual stream) is essentially zero at every token that matters, so this
program predicts 0 at every position. It is the honest answer because no
simple rule we tried predicts the activation:

- Its CI is ~0 everywhere (never above 0.1 in 10M tokens), and switching it
  off changes the model's next-token distribution by ~1e-6 nats per position.
- Its activation is ~0 at a document's first token (the MLP reads nothing
  there), and noisy elsewhere (std ~0.29, both signs, up to |4|).
- Token identity does not predict it (a per-token mean does worse than
  predicting 0 on held-out text), nor does a word-class split (verb,
  adjective/adverb, noun: all means within ±0.02 of 0).
- About 22% of its variance follows MLP hidden unit 1987 of the same layer
  (its weight on that unit is 0.35, the largest of its readout). That unit
  is itself positive on some code verbs ("execute", "view", "cat") and
  negative on some adverbs ("effectively", "merely"), but this is a weak,
  diffuse signal, not a rule a short program can follow.

Predicting 0 costs nothing measurable: the edited model's output KL is the
same as switching the component off.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """This component's activation at the newest position: always 0."""
    return carry, 0.0

"""Predict the component's typical activation: a constant near its average.

Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:1988 reads the MLP hidden state of layer 15 and
writes a small, dense contribution into the residual stream. Its activation is
roughly symmetric around 0 (mean 0.043, std 0.83) and no simple feature of the
text predicts it: the current token, the previous tokens, the position in the
document, the kind of text (code, maths, CJK, prose) and the running document
statistics each explain well under 1% of its variance. So the program predicts
the mean everywhere, which explains none of the variance and leaves the model's
output essentially unchanged, as switching the component off does.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.043


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """The component's activation at this position: its mean, whatever the prefix."""
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Predict zero everywhere.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:1989 is a near-dead rank-one piece of
layer 15's MLP down projection. Its activation is a small, roughly symmetric, diffuse value
(std about 0.3, typical magnitude about 0.24) with no token or position pattern that
predicts it: token identity explains about 2% of its variance on held-out data. Its causal
importance is almost always 0. So the simplest honest program predicts its mean, zero.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, 0.0

"""A word-level guess at component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:1990.

The component reads MLP hidden unit 1990 of layer 15 (about 0.55 of its 0.87 read norm
sits on that unit) and writes it into the residual stream. Its activation is large
and signed, and it is mostly context-dependent.

What this program does: it leans positive on connectives that open a time or event
clause or phrase ("after", "once", "upon", "following", "before", "during", "despite",
and some translations), about doubled when the connective follows a time span ("two
days after", "24 hours after"). It leans negative on "until", "while", "without", "per".
It gives a small bump to relative pronouns ("who", "those"), and sits at the component's
average (about -0.03) on every other token.

Why it is only a guess: word identity explains about 2% of its variance out of sample,
and a linear bag of the previous 16 tokens plus the current token about 1%. This program's
word table reaches about half a percent on eval, and switching it in changes the model's
output as little as switching the component off does.
"""

READS = ()

# Positive: connectives that introduce a time, event or concession phrase.
# Negative: "until", "while", "without", "per" (strongest on "per" and "without").
CONNECTIVES = {
    "after": 0.8, "once": 0.9, "upon": 0.5, "following": 0.5, "despite": 0.6,
    "before": 0.45, "during": 0.4, "amid": 0.5, "when": 0.2, "if": 0.15,
    "until": -0.3, "while": -0.2, "without": -0.35, "per": -0.4,
    "после": 1.0, "après": 0.9, "después": 0.7, "während": 0.8, "khi": 0.7,
    "一旦": 1.1, "随着": 0.9, "虽然": 0.7, "cuando": 0.5, "剛": 0.7, "刚": 0.9,
    "who": 0.4, "those": 0.4, "whose": 0.3, "whom": 0.2, "which": 0.1,
}

# Time spans that, just before a connective, roughly double its value ("days after").
TIME_SPANS = {"hours", "days", "minutes", "weeks", "seconds", "months", "years",
              "day", "week", "hour", "minute"}

# Value on every other token: the component's own average.
BASELINE = -0.03


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    value = CONNECTIVES.get(word, BASELINE)
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if same_doc and value != BASELINE and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() in TIME_SPANS:
        value *= 2.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection component 1991: a "fresh text" detector.

What it does, in plain terms: the component is silent on a document's first
token, rises over the first dozen or so tokens to a peak near position 12, and
then drifts down slowly through the rest of the document. Within that, it is
pushed up by a digit and pushed down by repetition: when the current token has
already occurred earlier in the same document, or when the current pair of
tokens (previous token, current token) has already occurred there. So it reads
high on new numbers and new wording, and low on text that copies earlier text.

The program is a linear rule over four readable features:
  * position in the document (log-scale curve, first token = 0),
  * the current token is a digit,
  * the current token already occurred earlier in this document,
  * the current two-token pair already occurred earlier in this document.
Coefficients were fit by least squares on training text. On held-out training
rows it explains about 10% of the activation's variance (eval: about 0.10).
What the simple rule leaves out: most of the remaining variance follows a slowly
changing context factor (for example, reasoning prose and copied code run low,
data-like tables run high) that no surface feature here captures.
"""

import math

import numpy as np

READS = ()

# Activation versus position in the document (log-spaced anchor points).
POSITIONS = [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512]
CURVE = [0.0, 4.4, 6.1, 7.2, 8.0, 8.4, 8.5, 8.3, 7.7, 6.9, 6.0, 5.2, 4.7]

BASE = 1.7  # intercept
POSITION_WEIGHT = 0.85  # scales the position curve
DIGIT_WEIGHT = 3.5  # the current token is a digit
TOKEN_REPEAT_WEIGHT = -1.2  # the current token occurred earlier in the document
PAIR_REPEAT_WEIGHT = -1.3  # the (previous, current) pair occurred earlier in the document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        # first token of a new document: positions and the repeat memory restart
        carry = (doc, 0, set(), set(), None)
    _, pos, tokens_seen, pairs_seen, previous = carry

    token = prefix.token_ids[-1]
    pair = (previous, token)
    if pos == 0:
        value = 0.0  # the first token of a document is silent
    else:
        curve = float(np.interp(math.log2(pos), [math.log2(p) for p in POSITIONS], CURVE))
        is_digit = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().isdigit()
        value = (
            BASE
            + POSITION_WEIGHT * curve
            + DIGIT_WEIGHT * is_digit
            + TOKEN_REPEAT_WEIGHT * (token in tokens_seen)
            + PAIR_REPEAT_WEIGHT * (pair in pairs_seen)
        )
    tokens_seen.add(token)
    pairs_seen.add(pair)
    return (doc, pos + 1, tokens_seen, pairs_seen, token), float(value)

"""Predicts the component's activation from the newest token's kind.

The component is a weak, diffuse part of the MLP output. Its activation depends on the
context in ways no token rule captures: token identity explains about 3% of its variance
out of sample, and the context windows add nothing. The one pattern that holds on training
rows is a difference in kind: alphabetic words average about 0.03, while punctuation,
digits, whitespace and other tokens average about 0.06 to 0.08. So the program predicts
those two means and nothing else.
"""

READS = ()

WORD_MEAN = 0.027
OTHER_MEAN = 0.07


def is_word(text):
    """An alphabetic word, with or without its leading space."""
    return text.strip().isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    return carry, WORD_MEAN if is_word(text) else OTHER_MEAN

"""layers.15 MLP unit 1993 (the component's input, which carries ~60% of its weight).

What it does: this unit is an "exception and contrast" detector. It is strongly positive on
words that introduce an exception, restriction or contrast ("except", "especially",
"although", "whereas", "including", and Chinese 其中 / 甚至 / 例如 / 但是), a little
positive on the word right after one, and on sentence and clause breaks (. ? ; : , ，).
It is negative on words that state a conclusion or a quantity or comparison
("respectively", "therefore", "hence", "thus", "since", "than", "if", "所以", "因此"),
and slightly negative on common prepositions ("of", "to", "in", "for", "by", ...).

The values are rough means read off training activations. The program captures only
about 2% of the activation's variance: the unit's activation depends on context well
beyond the current word, which a word list cannot see.
"""
READS = ()

# Words that introduce an exception, restriction or contrast, with typical activation.
EXCEPTION = {
    "except": 2.8, "exception": 2.5, "especially": 3.1, "particularly": 1.3, "particular": 0.9,
    "although": 1.8, "though": 1.3, "whereas": 1.9, "even": 0.5, "including": 1.1,
    "while": 0.4, "where": 0.6, "but": 0.6, "however": 0.2, "example": 0.6, "namely": 0.8,
    "其中": 5.4, "例如": 1.9, "甚至": 1.7, "但是": 1.1, "包括": 0.6, "但": 0.6,
}
# Words that state a conclusion, a comparison or a quantity: the unit is pushed down.
CONCLUSION = {
    "respectively": -0.75, "therefore": -0.6, "hence": -0.55, "thus": -0.5, "since": -0.3,
    "than": -0.3, "if": -0.25, "so": -0.2, "also": -0.25, "about": -0.25, "both": -0.3,
    "each": -0.2, "because": -0.2, "所以": -0.8, "因此": -0.7,
}
PREPOSITIONS = {"of", "to", "in", "for", "by", "from", "at", "as", "on", "this"}
# Sentence and clause breaks: weakly positive.
BREAKS = {".": 0.25, "?": 0.27, ";": 0.23, ":": 0.2, ",": 0.14, "，": 0.34, "\n\n": 0.24}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = raw.strip()
    if word in EXCEPTION:
        value = EXCEPTION[word]
    elif word in CONCLUSION:
        value = CONCLUSION[word]
    elif word in PREPOSITIONS:
        value = -0.1
    else:
        value = BREAKS.get(word, BREAKS.get(raw, 0.0))
    # The token right after an exception word is also raised a little.
    if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and prefix.token_strings[-2].strip() in EXCEPTION:
        value += 0.15
    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 1994, read through its down_proj component.

The component's input direction is almost entirely one hidden unit of the layer-15 MLP
(index 1994 has weight 0.87 in it; every other unit has about 0.04 or less). So its
activation is that unit's value, rescaled. That unit is only weakly tied to the words it
sits on, so this program is a rough, readable approximation: it predicts the few word
groups where the activation leans clearly one way, and a small lift inside tool calls.

- Strongly positive on the editor and shell tool-call words ("_editor", "view", "grep").
- Weakly positive on help, click and display text, and on tool-call JSON punctuation.
- Negative on form and button actions ("submit", "save", "update", "button").
- A small positive lift for every token inside a <tool_call> block.
- Otherwise about zero, the activation's mean.

The weights are least-squares fits to the activation on sampled training text.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

EDITOR_WORDS = frozenset({"_editor", "view", "grep"})
HELP_WORDS = frozenset({"help", "Help", "click", "show", "display", "echo"})
ACTION_WORDS = frozenset({"submit", "save", "update", "Update", "delete", "button", "Button", "btn"})
JSON_WORDS = frozenset({'",', '{"', "<tool_call>"})

EDITOR_WEIGHT = 1.6
HELP_WEIGHT = 0.2
ACTION_WEIGHT = -0.7
JSON_WEIGHT = 0.4
TOOL_CALL_WEIGHT = 0.12  # added to every token inside a <tool_call> block


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    in_tool, doc = carry if carry is not None else (False, None)
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:  # a new document starts: forget the tool-call state
        in_tool, doc = False, prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if "<tool_call>" in text:
        in_tool = True
    word = text.strip()
    value = TOOL_CALL_WEIGHT if in_tool else 0.0
    if word in EDITOR_WORDS:
        value += EDITOR_WEIGHT
    elif word in HELP_WORDS:
        value += HELP_WEIGHT
    elif word in ACTION_WORDS:
        value += ACTION_WEIGHT
    elif word in JSON_WORDS:
        value += JSON_WEIGHT
    if "</tool_call>" in text:
        in_tool = False
    return (in_tool, doc), float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 1995 (component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:1995).

What the component is: one rank-one write into the residual stream. Its input direction is
almost entirely MLP hidden unit 1995 of layer 15 (about 60% of its energy), so its activation
is that unit's value times the output norm. When the activation is negative, the write nudges
the next-token distribution toward words like "reduced", "lowered", "eliminated", "inhibit",
"rid" and "discourage"; when positive, it nudges the opposite way.

What predicts it: very little that can be read from text. Across 2 million training tokens,
the identity of the current token explains at most about 2% of its variance, a ridge fit on
bag-of-previous-8-tokens about 1%, and word lists for negation or reduction, repeated tokens
and repeated bigrams show no clear effect. Its large values (|activation| above 3, about 3 in
10,000 tokens) share no common word or topic I could find.

So this program predicts the typical value. Every position gets about -0.023, which is the
average over ordinary tokens; closing brackets and punctuation, the only classes whose average
differs visibly, get -0.05. The first token of each document gets 0, as the component does.
"""

READS = ()

CLOSERS = set("}])>,.;:!?\"'\\")
PLAIN = -0.023
CLOSER = -0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return None, 0.0
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if tok and tok[-1] in CLOSERS:
        return None, CLOSER
    return None, PLAIN

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 1997: a signed, diffuse readout with no simple concept.

What the component is: it reads the layer-15 MLP hidden vector (silu(gate) * up) along one
direction V[:,1997], scaled by the norm of its output vector U[1997]. Its own hidden unit,
MLP unit 1997, carries most of that direction, but the readout also sums thousands of small
contributions from other hidden units.

What was tried, and why this program is only a constant: its activation has mean about 0.01,
std 0.28, and is symmetric in sign. Neither the current token nor the previous token predicts
it (per-token means explain about 0% of the variance on held-out rows). Token classes (digits,
CJK, punctuation, newlines, capitals) and recent-window versions of them correlate under 0.02.
It is only weakly tied to position in the document. It does have slow context dependence (lag-1
autocorrelation about 0.28), and a linear fit on the normalized residual stream reaches about 0.2
variance explained, but that fit is a 1024-number table, not a readable rule.

So this program predicts the typical value everywhere, 0.0125, and explains about none of the
variance. Switching the component off changes the model's output very little, so a constant
keeps the model's behaviour unchanged.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TYPICAL_ACTIVATION = 0.0125


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, TYPICAL_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 1998: no readable concept found.

What the component is: one rank-one direction read from the MLP hidden state (6144 units)
and written back into the residual stream. Its activation is dense (std 0.84, spread
over both signs at every position), but it is not a simple function of anything a
person would name:
- the current token's identity explains about 1.5% of its variance (held out);
- position in the row, and position since the document started, explain about 0%;
- whether the token or the previous two tokens repeat earlier text explain about 0%;
- coarse lexical and code classes (digits, whitespace, punctuation, CJK, '=') explain
  under 0.2%;
- a linear map of all 2048 normalized residual dimensions explains about 17%, but that is
  2048 weights, not a readable rule, and no single residual dimension explains more than 0.3%.

So this program predicts the component's mean activation, 0, at every position. Switched
off, the component moves the model's next-token distribution by almost nothing (KL 1.4e-5
nats per position), and this program gives the same effect (kl_fraction 0.999).
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, 0.0

"""Copula-follower spikes for down_proj component 1999 of layer 15 (Qwen3-1.7B).

What it does: predicts a positive spike on the token right after a Chinese copula
(是 "is", 成为 "becomes", 作为 "as", 这是 "this is", 是一个 "is a") and the component's
mean activation everywhere else. The component's largest positive values sit on the
start of a predicate in formal Chinese prose, e.g. 是[全面]从严治党, 成为[...], 作为[...].

Why: copula positions carry many of the rare large positive activations (about 1 in 10
of the activations above 5 follows a copula, against about 1 in 5000 tokens overall).
But activations within |a| <= 1 hold about 85% of the squared deviation, a diffuse bulk
that depends on context the token text does not show. So this program explains very
little: on the eval rows its variance explained is about 0.001 and its Pearson r about
0.03, and its e2e effect is the same as switching the component off.

Scope: reads only the previous token's text and the document labels of the last two positions.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Copulas linking a subject to its predicate (token text, one token each).
COPULAS = {"是", "成为", "作为", "这是", "是一个"}
SPIKE = 0.7  # typical activation on the token after a copula
MEAN = -0.0226  # the component's mean activation everywhere else


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return None, MEAN  # no copula can precede a document's first token
    return None, SPIKE if prefix.token_strings[-2] in COPULAS else MEAN

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj component 2001: a diffuse, near-silent feature.

What it is: a single rank-one read of the layer-15 MLP hidden layer (its largest input weight
is on hidden unit 2001, about half its norm), writing a fixed direction into the residual stream.
Its activation is dense and roughly Gaussian (std about 0.3) with no token-level pattern:
the current token, the previous token, token classes (digits, words, punctuation, newlines,
Han characters) and slow context averages explain almost none of its variance. Switching it
off barely changes the model's predictions.

What this program captures: the one regularity found. The component is slightly positive on
the second token of each document and about zero on the first, and sits slightly below zero
everywhere else. Position inside a document is counted from the document's first token, and
resets where the document label changes.
"""

READS = ()

ELSEWHERE = -0.01  # the component's typical activation (its mean is about -0.01)
SECOND_TOKEN = 0.115  # its average on the second token of a document
FIRST_TOKEN = 0.0  # its average on the first token of a document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document label, position of the last token in that document), or None at a row start
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        pos = 0
    else:
        pos = carry[1] + 1
    if pos == 0:
        value = FIRST_TOKEN
    elif pos == 1:
        value = SECOND_TOKEN
    else:
        value = ELSEWHERE
    return (doc, pos), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2002: a near-constant, mostly unexplained signal.

What the component is: one rank-one piece of the layer-15 MLP down projection. It reads
the MLP hidden vector through a direction that is mostly one hidden unit (unit 2002,
about 46% of its variance), and writes along a fixed output direction. Its activation is
dense and noisy: mean about -0.067, std about 0.42, with heavy tails in both signs.

What this program does: it predicts the two things that are reliable.
  * At the first token of each document (including the first token of a packed row) the
    component is silent: its activation is about 0.
  * Everywhere else it sits at its typical level, about -0.067.

What it does not do: it does not explain the spikes. Their sign and size depend on the
hidden state, and token identity, previous token, bag of recent tokens, position and
token repetition each explain almost none of them (held-out R^2 under 0.01). So the
program explains about 0 of the variance; its value is in the document-start rule and
in the honest baseline. Switching the component off changes the model's next-token
output by almost nothing (KL 2.6e-6 nats per position), so the component is close to
inert.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

TYPICAL = -0.067  # the component's typical activation on ordinary tokens


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # A new document starts here: the first token of the row, or the first token of a
    # document packed partway through a row (the model resets attention there too).
    new_document = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if new_document else TYPICAL

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection component 2003: the "by means of" feature.

What it does: it fires on the word that introduces HOW something is done, the
means or method, as in "analysed by ...", "performed by ...", "removed by
clicking", "via", "through", "using", "par", "por", "durch". Its output direction
promotes "method / using / by means of" continuations, so it is a means-marker.

Plain rules used here:
- "by" is strongly positive (about 5), except in fixed or mathematical frames
  such as "divided by", "multiplied by", "followed by", "caused by", "posted by",
  "step by step", where it stays near 0.
- The word right after a means-"by" (the "the" or the gerund) is weakly positive.
- Other means words ("through", "via", "using", "par", "por", "durch", ...) are
  moderately positive.
- Place and time prepositions ("in", "at", "from", "with", "as", ...) are
  weakly negative.
Everything else is predicted as 0. The rules explain only about 12% of the
variance, because most of the activation is diffuse background that no simple
word or context rule captures.
"""

READS = ()

MEANS_WORDS = {"through", "via", "using", "par", "por", "durch", "mediante", "prin", "use"}
FIXED_OR_MATH = {"divided", "multiplied", "multiply", "divisible", "sides", "times",
                 "followed", "caused", "posted", "inspired", "characterized", "step", "class"}
PLACE_TIME = {"in", "at", "from", "with", "as", "within", "during"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token, from the word itself and the word before it."""
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""
    if word == "by":
        return None, (0.7 if prev in FIXED_OR_MATH else 4.8)
    if prev == "by":
        return None, 1.1
    if word in MEANS_WORDS:
        return None, 1.1
    if word in PLACE_TIME:
        return None, -0.2
    return None, 0.0

"""Explainer for layers.15.mlp.down_proj:2005 in Qwen3-1.7B.

The component's activation is large and signed. Three things readable from the
text set most of it, and the program is the sum of them:

1. Position in the document. The first token of a document gives 0. From the
   second token on the value is high (about +13 to +15) and falls with the log
   of the distance from the document start, by about 1.5 per doubling, reaching
   zero roughly 600 tokens in.
2. Repetition. A token that already occurred earlier in the same document is
   pushed down by about 3.7; a token seen for the first time is not.
3. Kind of token. Indentation runs and code punctuation are pushed down; words
   in other alphabets (Greek, Cyrillic, CJK) are pushed up; plain Latin words
   sit in between.

This explains about 19% of the variance on eval rows (r about 0.43).
The rest depends on context the token features do not capture.
"""

import math
import re
import unicodedata

READS = ()

# Activation at distance d from the document start (d >= 1): a + b * log2(d).
# Kind weights are relative to a plain Latin word.
CURVE_A = 14.1
CURVE_B = -1.5

# Added for each kind of token (see token_kind).
KIND_WEIGHT = {
    "indent": -2.2,
    "newline": 0.5,
    "space": 1.0,
    "digits": 0.7,
    "punct": -0.5,
    "word": 0.0,
    "mixed": -0.5,
    "script": 1.7,
}

# Added when the token already occurred earlier in its document.
REPEAT_WEIGHT = -3.7


def token_kind(s):
    """A coarse kind of token, from its text alone."""
    if not s.strip():
        if "\n" in s:
            return "newline"
        return "indent" if len(s) >= 2 else "space"
    letters = [c for c in s if c.isalpha()]
    if not letters:
        return "digits" if any(c.isdigit() for c in s) else "punct"
    if re.fullmatch(r" ?[A-Za-z]+", s):
        return "word"
    if all(unicodedata.name(c, "").startswith("LATIN") for c in letters):
        return "mixed"
    return "script"


def update(carry, document_id, token_id, token_string):
    """Track position in the document and the tokens seen so far in it.

    Returns the new carry and the features of this token: its position in
    its document, its kind, and whether it repeats an earlier token there.
    """
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document_id:
        pos, seen = 0, set()
    else:
        pos, seen = carry[1] + 1, carry[2]
    repeat = token_id in seen
    seen.add(token_id)
    kind = token_kind(token_string)
    return (document_id, pos, seen), pos, kind, repeat


def predict(pos, kind, repeat):
    """The component's activation predicted from those features."""
    if pos == 0:
        return 0.0
    curve = CURVE_A + CURVE_B * math.log2(pos)
    return curve + KIND_WEIGHT[kind] + (REPEAT_WEIGHT if repeat else 0.0)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    carry, pos, kind, repeat = update(
        carry,
        prefix.document_ids[-1],
        prefix.token_ids[-1],
        prefix.token_strings[-1],
    )
    return carry, predict(pos, kind, repeat)

direction is almost entirely that unit (V's weight on it is 0.70), and its

unit's value.

What a short rule can say about it: the unit leans positive on words that
point at a displayed item, such as "shown", "below", "following", "Figure",
"Table", "diagram", and most strongly on the word itself. Its value is higher
when such words occurred in the last 30 tokens of the same document. Its
activation is otherwise diffuse, small and context dependent, which no short
word list captures, so this program explains only a small part of its variance.

Predicted value at each token:
  0.5 if the token is a display-reference word,
  plus 0.05 for each earlier display-reference word in the last 30 tokens of
  the same document (at most 4 of them).

READS = ()

DISPLAY_WORDS = frozenset(
    {
        "figure", "figures", "fig", "table", "diagram", "chart", "graph",
        "schematic", "below", "above", "shown", "shows", "show", "following",
        "follows", "given", "indicated", "displayed", "illustrated", "depicted",
        "here",
    }
)
WINDOW = 30
WORD_VALUE = 0.5
CONTEXT_VALUE = 0.05
CONTEXT_CAP = 4


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Carry: (document label, positions of recent display-reference words)."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    t = prefix.position
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, [])

    return (doc, recent), float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP unit 2009 (down_proj component 2009), as a short rule.

What it is: this component reads essentially one MLP hidden unit of layer 15 and writes
along a direction that promotes words like "limit", "infinity", "undefined", "endpoints",
"critical", "invalid", "∞". It is active in math reasoning about limits, asymptotes,
excluded values and where an expression is zero, positive, negative or undefined
("x ≠ -2", "approaching 1", "vertical asymptotes", "the slope is undefined"). It is near
zero in most prose and code. Its largest values often sit on the word or token just before
a boundary value.

What the rule does, from the prefix only, with three word classes:
  - BOUNDARY: limit / asymptote / ≠ / ∞ / undefined / zero / domain / interval ...
  - CONNECTIVE: So, Thus, Therefore, Hence (they open a deduction);
  - SIGN: roots, solutions, positive, negative, real, between, ⇒, <, >, ...
and a running level `s` of recent talk in these classes (decays by 0.9 per token, reset at
each document start). The value is
    1.4 * CONNECTIVE + 0.15 * BOUNDARY + 0.15 * s
  + 2.3 * BOUNDARY * s + 0.7 * CONNECTIVE * s + 0.5 * SIGN * s.
A boundary word inside such talk is what drives the large values.

The coefficients are least-squares fits on training rows. The rule explains only about 2–3%
of the variance. The rest sits in context these word classes don't capture: a GRU on the full
prefix tokens reaches about 0.1 on held-out rows, and a GRU on coarse token classes only
about 0.03. A token-identity table of the 1000 most-used tokens reaches about 0.03.
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

BOUNDARY = re.compile(
    r"\s*(≠|∞|infty|infinity|infinite|asympt\w*|limit\w*|approach\w*|undefined|singular|"
    r"discontin\w*|critical|endpoints?|exclud\w*|except|cannot|invalid|domain|intervals?|"
    r"zero|unbounded)\s*$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
CONNECTIVE = re.compile(r"\s*(so|thus|therefore|hence)\s*[,.]?$", re.IGNORECASE)
SIGN = re.compile(
    r"\s*(positive|negative|zero|roots?|solutions?|real|between|none|only|integers?|"
    r"≤|≥|<|>|=|⇒|→|<=|>=)\s*$",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
DECAY = 0.9


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # carry: (talk level before this token, document of the previous token)
    level, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else (0.0, None)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if doc != last_doc:
        level = 0.0  # a new document: forget the earlier talk
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    b = BOUNDARY.match(token) is not None
    c = CONNECTIVE.match(token) is not None
    g = SIGN.match(token) is not None
    value = 1.4 * c + 0.15 * b + 0.15 * level + 2.3 * b * level + 0.7 * c * level + 0.5 * g * level
    talk = 1.0 if (b or c or g) else 0.0
    return (DECAY * level + talk, doc), float(value)

What it responds to, as far as a token list can tell: generic placeholder

"""Milestone-"first" detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj, component 2011.

What the component does: when it is strongly negative it pushes the residual stream toward
words like "first", "pioneering", "unprecedented", "unique" and "ever" (its output direction,
read through the unembedding). So it is a "this is a historic first / record" feature that
is negative on the words that set up such a milestone: "became the" (as in "became the
[first/youngest/only]"), "the first" (in "the first woman", "for the first time"), "the only",
"the largest", and the end of a document.

The program writes that down as plain rules over the text so far:
  - "the/a/an" right after "became/become/becomes/becoming": strongly negative.
  - "first": negative (about -1.4 on average; more negative when a milestone word is nearby).
  - a milestone word (only, largest, woman, ...) within 8 tokens of a milestone word: negative.
  - end-of-text: negative (about -1.4 on average).
Everything else is 0. The values are the average activations of each rule, rounded.
Measured: explains under 1% of the variance (the activation is spread over many contexts and
rare large negative spikes); switching it off changes the output about as much as this does.

READS = ()

BECOME = {"became", "become", "becomes", "becoming"}
ARTICLES = {"the", "a", "an"}
MILESTONE = {
    "first", "only", "youngest", "oldest", "largest", "biggest", "highest", "lowest",
    "unprecedented", "pioneer", "pioneering", "history", "record", "woman", "became",
    "become", "becomes", "elected", "ever", "unique",
}

    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""
    # Is a milestone word among the 8 tokens before this one?

    milestone_context = bool(window & MILESTONE)

    elif cur == "<|endoftext|>":
        value = -1.4
    elif cur in MILESTONE and milestone_context:
        value = -2.5
    else:

    return carry, float(value)

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2014: a negative "turn boundary / line break" detector.

What it does: the component is near zero on most tokens and goes strongly negative on a few
kinds of token, mainly
  * chat-turn markers and role names (<|im_start|>, <|im_end|>, user, assistant, <tool_call>...),
  * line breaks, above all a line break that comes right after a turn marker (the newline in
    "<|im_start|>user\\n" or "<|im_end|>\\n"),
  * weaker negatives on line breaks, punctuation and words, strongest in the first few tokens
    of a document and fading with distance from its start.
The program predicts the mean activation for each (token kind, previous token kind, distance
from the document start) cell, as measured on training text. It keeps two numbers of state
per row: the distance from the document's start and the kind of the previous token.
"""

import re

TURN = re.compile(r"\s*(</?[\w|]+>|user|assistant|system|speaker)\s*")
END = re.compile(r".*[.!?。！？;:}\])\"]\s*")
WORD = re.compile(r"\s*([A-Za-z]+|\d+)\s*")

READS = ()

TURN_KIND, NEWLINE_KIND, PUNCT_KIND, WORD_KIND, OTHER_KIND = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4

# Mean activation by (token kind, previous token's group) and distance from document start
# bucket: <4, 4-15, 16-63, 64+ tokens. Groups: 0 after a turn marker, 1 after a line break,
# 2 after anything else. Rounded values fitted on 4096 training rows.
TABLE = {
    (0, 0): (-4.6, -1.3, -3.6, -5.2),  # turn marker after turn marker
    (0, 1): (-1.4, 0.3, 0.4, 0.2),  # turn marker after line break
    (0, 2): (-2.9, -4.4, -3.6, -1.4),  # turn marker after other text
    (1, 0): (-6.8, -7.3, -7.4, -6.2),  # line break after turn marker: strongest
    (1, 1): (-0.7, -0.9, -1.4, -1.3),  # line break after line break
    (1, 2): (-1.0, -2.8, -2.6, -1.0),  # line break after other text
    (2, 0): (0.0, -0.3, -1.4, -0.7),  # sentence/clause end after turn marker
    (2, 1): (-3.2, -1.6, -1.0, -0.4),  # sentence/clause end after line break
    (2, 2): (-1.2, -2.2, -1.5, -0.3),  # sentence/clause end after other text
    (3, 0): (-6.7, -4.4, -2.8, -0.5),  # word after turn marker
    (3, 1): (-1.8, -1.3, -2.0, -1.4),  # word after line break
    (3, 2): (-1.6, -0.9, -0.2, 0.0),  # word after other text
    (4, 0): (0.6, -2.2, 0.0, -0.0),  # other token after turn marker
    (4, 1): (-0.3, -0.8, -1.4, -0.6),  # other token after line break
    (4, 2): (-1.7, -1.5, -0.5, -0.0),  # other token after other text
}


def token_kind(s):
    """Kind of one token, from its decoded text."""
    if TURN.fullmatch(s):
        return TURN_KIND
    if "\n" in s:
        return NEWLINE_KIND
    if s.strip() and END.fullmatch(s):
        return PUNCT_KIND
    if WORD.fullmatch(s):
        return WORD_KIND
    return OTHER_KIND


def distance_bucket(d):
    """0 for under 4 tokens into the document, then 1 for under 16, 2 for under 64, 3 beyond."""
    return 0 if d < 4 else 1 if d < 16 else 2 if d < 64 else 3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """Activation at the newest token. carry = (tokens since document start, kind of newest token)."""
    kind = token_kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if carry is None or new_doc:
        distance, previous = 0, None
    else:
        distance, previous = carry[0] + 1, carry[1]
    if distance == 0:
        value = 0.0  # a document's first token is always about zero
    else:
        group = {TURN_KIND: 0, NEWLINE_KIND: 1}.get(previous, 2)
        value = TABLE[(kind, group)][distance_bucket(distance)]
    return (distance, kind), float(value)

"""

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2016: a diffuse, near-inert readout.

What it is: the component reads the layer-15 MLP hidden vector through one

    "opener": (1.35, -1.20),   # token ends in an opening bracket
    "quote": (0.55, -0.10),    # token contains a quote character
    "newline": (0.12, 0.05),   # text with a line break

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 2036: a weak, position-driven feature.

What it does: this component's activation is near zero at the first token of a
document, rises over the first ~20 tokens to a plateau of about 0.6, and then fades
slowly, to about 0.05 by token 400 of the document. Within that, it is a diffuse,
largely unpredictable signal: its values scatter widely (std about 1.2, with rare
spikes up to 30) around the position profile, and no token identity, token class
or repetition explains them. So this program predicts the average profile by
position in the document, plus a small bump on whitespace-only tokens, which carry
slightly higher activation on average. It does not explain the spikes.

Position is counted from the start of each document; the carry keeps the count and
the document label, so the program does not re-read the prefix.

import math

READS = ()

PEAK_AT = 20          # tokens into a document where the profile peaks
PEAK = 0.6            # its height
FADE = 120.0          # tokens for the profile to fade by a factor of e, after the peak
SPACE_BUMP = 0.1      # extra on whitespace-only tokens (no newline)


def profile(n):
    """Mean activation n tokens into a document: a ramp up, then a slow fade."""
    if n < PEAK_AT:
        return PEAK * n / PEAK_AT
    return PEAK * math.exp(-(n - PEAK_AT) / FADE)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[1] != doc:
        n = 0                      # first token of a new document
    else:
        n = carry[0] + 1
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = profile(n)
    if token.strip() == "" and "\n" not in token:
        value += SPACE_BUMP
    return (n, doc), value

It writes almost nothing into the residual stream (its causal importance is ~0 on every
token), and its activation has no clear token-level pattern: a token's identity explains
only a few percent of its variance, and the rest depends on context this program cannot
see. What regularities there are:

- At a document's first token it is essentially 0.
- On closing chat-markup tags (</tool_call>, </tool_response>) and <think>, <|im_end|>,
  it is clearly negative.
- On runs of rule-like symbols (====, ----, ____, @@) and on separator punctuation
  (. - _ / ] :) it is mildly negative.
- Everywhere else it is a small, noisy, slightly negative value.

new document has started, so it needs no carried state.

from collections.abc import Mapping

RULE_RUN = re.compile(r"\s*[=\-_@*#~+]{3,}\s*")
SEPARATORS = {".", "-", "_", "/", "]", ":", ".\n", ".\n\n"}

TAG_MEAN = -0.44
RULE_MEAN = -0.18
SEPARATOR_MEAN = -0.08
OTHER_MEAN = -0.02


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    if t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[t] != prefix.document_ids[t - 1]:
        return carry, 0.0  # first token of a document: the component is silent
    s = prefix.token_strings[t]
    if s in CHAT_TAGS:

    if RULE_RUN.fullmatch(s):

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 2039 (component 2039 of down_proj), read as a forum-page detector.

The component is essentially one MLP hidden unit: its activation is that unit's value times
its output norm. The unit goes strongly negative inside the boilerplate of web-forum pages:
the user-profile sidebar and post headers ("Joined:", "Posts:", "Own Kudos", "Tags", "Views",
"Posted by", "Originally Posted by", "Thread", "Forum", dates like "Aug 20, 2010"). Its
output, when negative, pushes the model toward predicting such labels (its logit-lens top
tokens include " Thread" and "Joined").

This program predicts the activation from two running counts that reset at each document:
  label:  a decayed count of forum/page-furniture words and month names just read
  marks:  a decayed count of metadata formatting just read (numbers, colons, bullets,

about zero. The program does not reproduce the model's computation: it is a readable
stand-in that captures the forum-block pattern, not the exact per-token magnitudes.

SCALE = -0.4  # activation per unit of label * marks, fitted on training rows

FORUM_WORDS = frozenset(
    """posted originally joined posts post views view replies reply tags tag thread topic
    forum member members club kudos permalink mechanics expert homework board directors
    follow show help related comment locked likes liked given thanks edited quote wrote user
    sort hide status moderator school display helper statement staff""".split()
)
MONTHS = frozenset("jan feb mar apr may jun jul aug sep sept oct nov dec".split())
MARKS = frozenset([":", "•", "#", "##", "###"])


def is_label(token):
    """A word of forum or web-page furniture, or a month name from a post date."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    return word in FORUM_WORDS or word in MONTHS


def is_mark(token):
    """Metadata formatting: a number, a colon or bullet, a '#' header, or a line break."""
    text = token.strip()
    return text.isdigit() or text in MARKS or "\n" in token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

projection of the MLP's 6144 hidden units onto one direction, so it has no single

about 3% of its variance on held-out text, and coarse word classes explain well under
1%. Switching it off changes the model's next-token predictions by about 1e-6 nats.

plain terms:

  * position in its document: the second token runs high (about +0.11), tokens 3 to 16

  * the kind of token: newlines run low, digits and punctuation a little low, Chinese

the document label changes, as the model resets attention and positions.

    "partial": 0.016,
    "space": -0.003,
    "newline": -0.036,
    "cjk": 0.019,
    "word": 0.007,
    "digits": -0.020,
    "punct": -0.019,
    "mixed": 0.003,

def position_bucket(p):

    if p <= 15:

    if p <= 63:

    if re.search(r"[一-鿿]", core):
        return "cjk"
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z]+", core):

    if re.fullmatch(r"\d+", core):

entirely that unit), scaled by the length of its output vector. The unit is quiet on most

* Negative values on a digit that follows a decimal point ("2.[6]"), strongest when the
  last 20 tokens mention a statistic (mean, median, %, +/-, patients, ...), as in reported
  results such as "mean age was 65.7 months".
* Mild positive values on code structure: indentation runs and tokens with ';', '{', '}'.

the unit's activity is diffuse and not predictable from the token or its nearby context.

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

STATISTIC = re.compile(r"mean|median|average|SD|±|%|patients|CI|ratio", re.IGNORECASE)
CODE_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[;{}]|[ \t]{2,}")
DECIMAL_DIGIT = -0.9  # a digit after a decimal point
STATISTIC_DECIMAL_DIGIT = -2.5  # the same, with a statistic in the last 20 tokens
CODE_TOKEN_VALUE = 0.12  # indentation or statement punctuation


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    doc = prefix.document_ids
    cur = tokens[-1]
    # The tokens before this one, back to the start of its document (at most 21).
    back = []
    for k in range(2, min(len(tokens), 22) + 1):
        if doc[-k] != doc[-1]:

        back.append(tokens[-k])
    prev = back[0] if back else ""
    prev2 = back[1] if len(back) > 1 else ""
    if re.fullmatch(r"\d", cur) and (prev == "." or (prev2 == "." and prev.isdigit())):

            return carry, STATISTIC_DECIMAL_DIGIT
        return carry, DECIMAL_DIGIT
